findings.suggested_fix: Say in T-11 that the MVP actor is always 'staff', so who did it is not recorded until sign-in exists. Move T-11 from 'covered by existing controls' to a stated, accepted gap that this change does not widen.
findings.text: T-11 says appointment_event records who made each change. In the MVP every actor is the fixed 'staff', so events cannot tell staff members apart. The repudiation threat is still open, not covered by an existing control.

findings.suggested_fix: Either describe these as integrity risks with a clear security consequence, or note them as non-security quality risks passed on to the implement step's tests.
findings.text: T-5 (API and web type drift) and T-12 (shared-rule regression) are correctness risks with no attacker, labelled as STRIDE tampering. This makes the threat list look broader than its real security content.

rubric_items.reason: All nine design components (CO-1 to CO-9) appear as threat components with at least one threat each. The endpoint changes are covered through CO-1 (T-3, T-14).
Most threats fit their component, for example T-1 on spreading a DoctorSummary that holds phone and email. T-5 and T-12 are correctness or regression risks labelled as tampering.
Mitigations are either cited existing controls or clearly stated new controls (T-1, T-5). T-11 overstates what appointment_event proves in the MVP, and T-8 relies on C7, which does not apply.

T-3 states the MVP gap where every permission is granted, but Known still lists T-3 as covered. The repudiation gap (every actor is 'staff') is not stated. Assumed, Unknown and Open questions are all empty.
Readable, and the frontmatter matches the body. Threats are grouped by component with no risk rating, so they are not ordered by risk.
